Oliver — thanks for the clear summary and the redlines. I appreciate the urgency.

Short answer: we can move forward but need executive authorization for changes to the liability cap and broader indemnity language. I'll escalate now and propose a path that preserves the pilot economics while addressing their legal concerns.

Proposed path (for our internal review):
- Counter-propose a $2M liability cap tied to aggregate subscription fees for the 12-month term rather than a flat $5M.
- Require Bluestone to provide an updated insurance certificate showing $5M per-occurrence coverage and name Redwood as additional insured for the pilot term.
- Accept IP indemnity on a limited scope (claims arising from Bluestone's use of the service) with explicit carveouts for third-party models or data they bring.
- Approve a one-time commercial concession (15% off first-year subscription fees) contingent on signature of the attached amendment and receipt of insurance cert.

I'll loop in Ben, Markus, and Steph for final exec/finance/legal agreement. Can we schedule a 30-min call tomorrow (Sep 15) to iron details?

Thanks — Jasmine

Team — quick escalation. Bluestone (prospect) sent redlines requesting a mutual $5M cap and broader indemnity provisions; they're also asking for a 22% first-year discount because of the risk they're adding. Details attached (Bluestone_Redline_v1.docx).

Summary of risk & commercial impact:
- ARR for pilot: $480k ARR (12-month term = $480k total committed).
- Proposed 22% discount reduces first-year revenue to ~ $375k. Our counter suggested 15% (one-time concession) + insurance verification.
- Legal asks: broader IP indemnity and warranty tightening to 60 days.

Requests:
1) Exec sign-off on liability cap change: propose $2M aggregate cap (not per-occurrence) tied to subscription fees.
2) Approve 15% one-time commercial concession conditional on delivery of certificate of insurance naming Redwood as additional insured with $5M per-occurrence coverage.
3) Agreement that IP indemnity remains limited to claims arising from Bluestone’s use of Redwood (no broad customer-sourced model indemnity).

If approved, I will issue Amendment_X1_for_Bluestone.docx for signature and coordinate DocuSign.

Why the approach: lowers our exposure while meeting procurement halfway (insurance + discount). Without approval, we risk losing the pilot.

Please reply with Approve / Approve with changes / Decline. If Approve with changes, list them.

Thanks — Jasmine

Jasmine — thanks for the clear ask and the proposed mitigation. I agree with the approach with one amendment.

Decision: APPROVE with conditions.
Conditions to be satisfied before legal executes amendment:
1) Liability cap: approve $2,000,000 aggregate cap for the 12-month pilot (aggregate subscription fees capped at $480k, so cap is ~4.2x ARR — acceptable for pilot).
2) Insurance: Bluestone must provide an ACORD-style certificate showing at least $5M per-occurrence/aggregate for general liability and technology errors & omissions (E&O). They must name Redwood Inference as additional insured for the pilot period and provide primary, non-contributory wording where available. Receipt of policy plus a point-of-contact at their broker is required.
3) Indemnity: accept IP indemnity narrowly scoped to claims arising from Bluestone’s use of our service (explicitly exclude claims related to models/data they supply).
4) Warranty window: we will not accept a warranty shorter than 90 days for services; counter to 90 days instead of their 60 days.
5) Commercial concession: authorize 15% off first-year fees (one-time) once insurance and amendment are signed.

Markus (cc'd) — finance/legal, please confirm if the 15% is acceptable to revenue recognition accounting and that operations is okay with insurance requirements.

If all good, Jasmine, proceed to send Amendment_X1_for_Bluestone.docx and load DocuSign link.

Ben
VP, North America Sales | Redwood Inference
